transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-30
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood Security SE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Amelia Stone (Pinegrove CISO), Diego Ramos (IT Director), Priya Mehta (Compliance Manager), Liam O'Connor (DevOps)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood. Uh Samira and Marcus from security and solutions are with me. Appreciate you carving out the time for a SOC 2 / ISO posture review.
[00:18] Amelia Stone: Thanks Jordan. We have a pretty aggressive compliance calendar, so we wanted to go over your latest attestations, trust center access, and specific controls mapping to ISO 27001. Also want to understand your RBAC, SSO, KMS story for production keys.
[00:34] Samira Patel: Absolutely. Quick agenda: share high-level of our SOC 2 Type II & ISO scope, show where the artifacts live in the Trust Center, talk KMS options (customer-managed keys, HSM, bring-your-own), RBAC/SSO and audit logs, then capture any gaps and next steps.
[00:48] Diego Ramos: Great. One thing up front: encryption in transit is table stakes, but we need to know how customer data at rest is isolated when using Redwood Dedicated vs Redwood Private.
[01:05] Marcus Chen: Right, good question. For Redwood Dedicated we isolate tenant compute and storage at the VM and storage layer; encryption at rest uses provider-managed keys by default, but we support customer-managed keys (CMK) through KMS with HSM-backed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments.
[01:25] Priya Mehta: And do you have a documented KMS key rotation policy and proof in the SOC 2 evidence? We need to map that to A.10.1 in ISO 27001.
[01:40] Samira Patel: Yes, key rotation is covered in our cryptographic controls evidence. We'll share the relevant control file. Note that the SOC 2 redacted report references our key management controls and rotation cadence; the Trust Center has the redacted artifacts.
[01:57] Liam O'Connor: On the SSO side, we use SAML + SCIM for provisioning. Does Redwood support SCIM for user sync and groups so we can enforce RBAC via our IdP?
[02:12] Jordan Lee: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is role-based with tenancy-level roles plus custom roles on Private deployments. There are a few caveats around API admin rights we can go through.
[02:30] Amelia Stone: Sounds good. Can you clarify audit log retention windows and whether logs are tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody type assurances for eDiscovery requests.
[02:46] Samira Patel: Audit logs are stored with append-only semantics in our logging pipeline. For Hosted we retain 90 days by default, with paid add-ons for longer retention; Dedicated/Private deployments can configure retention to meet compliance. We can provide attestations and the logging architecture diagram from the Trust Center.
[03:07] Diego Ramos: Do you push logs to customer-owned S3 buckets or can we pull them via an audit API?
[03:15] Marcus Chen: Both. We have a push connector to customer S3/GCS for Dedicated and Private; we also expose an audit logs API with signed requests. We'll note the delivery options in the controls mapping doc.
[03:30] Amelia Stone: OK. Regarding scope: is your SOC 2 Type II covering the entire Redwood platform or just hosted API? We need to know which controls apply to Dedicated and Private.
[03:44] Samira Patel: The current SOC 2 Type II covers our hosted service and control plane in scope; Dedicated has overlapping controls but some operational aspects (customer-managed infra) are not in our SOC scope. For Private deployments, customers operate the infrastructure so their own SOC/ISO controls apply. We'll provide a cut-and-dry mapping that shows which controls are Redwood-managed vs customer-managed.
[04:10] Priya Mehta: That's key for us because our auditors will want to see shared responsibility. If you can provide a clear matrix it makes our life easier.
[04:20] Jordan Lee: Totally agree. We'll include a controls matrix mapping Redwood controls to SOC 2/ISO clauses and highlight customer responsibilities.
[04:32] [05:00] Marcus Chen: Quick note on penetration testing and vulnerability disclosure: we run annual pen tests plus continuous fuzzing and we have a public vuln disclosure policy. We can share last pen test summary redacted for customer review.
[05:18] Amelia Stone: We'd like to see the pen test summary, scope, and remediation timelines. Also does Redwood do third-party vendor assessments for cloud providers?
[05:30] Samira Patel: Yes, we have vendor risk management, and our vendor list and criticality assessments are part of the Trust Center. We use major CSPs and maintain their compliance artifact links.
[05:42] Diego Ramos: On data residency — we operate entirely in the EU for some workloads. Can you guarantee data residency (at rest) for EU-only customers on Redwood Hosted?
[05:55] Marcus Chen: For Hosted, we can route and pin workloads to EU regions and ensure persistent storage is in EU. We also have Dedicated and Private options if you need guaranteed material control. We'll need the list of required regions so we can confirm exact availability and any extra contractual terms.
[06:18] Priya Mehta: Good. Also, about evidence: auditors will likely ask for network diagrams, change management logs, user access reviews, and least privilege proof. Can you provide sample artifacts?
[06:30] Samira Patel: Yes, sample artifacts are in the Trust Center. We'll send a collection of redacted evidence packs: network diagram, change mgmt ticket samples, privileged access review snapshots, and our regular audit schedule.
[06:45] Jordan Lee: Real quick, any blockers or must-haves from Pinegrove that would prevent you from moving forward?
[06:52] Amelia Stone: Two things: detailed controls mapping and clarification on KMS/CMK options plus audit logs export to our S3. If those are satisfied, we can include Redwood in our vendor security review and move to contract discussions.
[07:10] Jordan Lee: Understood. We'll prioritize those docs.
[07:15] [07:30] Marcus Chen: I want to flag a minor nuance — when using CMK in Dedicated, some metadata like request logs are still processed in our control plane; we can provide an architecture note and options for additional isolation if required.
[07:45] Liam O'Connor: That's fine as long as the sensitive payloads are encrypted with CMK and we can run key rotation and revoke access if needed.
[07:56] Samira Patel: Correct, payloads are encrypted client-side when customers use the client-side encryption flow; with server-side CMK the data at rest is protected but certain metadata remains in the control plane. We'll document trade-offs.
[08:12] Diego Ramos: About SSO provisioning and groups: can you map SCIM groups to Redwood roles so engineers get the right permissions automatically?
[08:22] Marcus Chen: Yes, SCIM group-to-role mapping is supported. For Hosted customers we offer a pre-defined role set; for Dedicated/Private we support custom role creation and SCIM mappings.
[08:35] Amelia Stone: Will SCIM push deprovisions be immediate? Auditors will ask about orphaned accounts.
[08:42] Samira Patel: Push deprovisions are near-real-time — within a minute in most cases — and we include proof in our access governance artifacts.
[08:55] [09:20] Jordan Lee: Any questions about contractual items like SOC 2 addendum or data processing addendum (DPA)?
[09:27] Priya Mehta: We'll need a DPA and a SOC 2 addendum that references processing locations, subprocessors, and the security incident response SLA.
[09:36] Jordan Lee: We have standard DPAs and can add specific residency clauses for EU, we'll share templates.
[09:43] Marcus Chen: Also to call out: for Private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM on prem and keep keys fully out of Redwood's control.
[09:53] Amelia Stone: That option might be our preference for PHI workloads.
[10:00] Samira Patel: Understood. We'll provide documentation on on-prem KMS integration and a short checklist for initial setup.
[10:12] Diego Ramos: One practical ask — can Redwood give us a mapping file showing which SOC 2 control IDs map to ISO 27001 clauses? A simple CSV would help.
[10:22] Jordan Lee: Yes, Samira will prepare a controls mapping CSV and an executive summary for auditors.
[10:28] [10:45] Priya Mehta: Good. Timeline-wise, our procurement window is mid-Jan, so if we have artifacts in the first two weeks of Jan we'll be in good shape.
[10:54] Jordan Lee: We'll commit to that.
[11:00] Marcus Chen: Quick clarification on audit log integrity: we use a write-once datastore for logs with signed checksums; we can provide a technical note and sample checksum outputs.
[11:12] Amelia Stone: Excellent. That addresses chain of custody.
[11:20] [11:45] Jordan Lee: To recap the action items: Redwood will share Trust Center link + SOC2 redacted report, controls mapping CSV, pen test summary, KMS docs and audit log delivery options. Pinegrove will send region/residency requirements and confirm timeline. We'll set a follow-up technical deep dive for KMS and logs.
[12:05] Amelia Stone: Sounds right. Thank you everyone.
[12:10] Jordan Lee: Thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the deep dive.
[12:20] [12:45] End meeting

Notes about transcript quality: Occasional transcription errors / product names slightly mis-heard (e.g., 'Redwood Privatee' / 'Reedwood'), filler words and short crosstalk present.

References shared during call: Trust Center (link provided post-call), redacted SOC 2 Type II report, controls mapping CSV (to be delivered), pen test summary (redacted).
